I am 60 this year, and I have farmed these same 6 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years. I finished high school, so I keep a small notebook tracking yields and input costs, and I talk with the county ag technician when he visits the village. I also check weather alerts on my phone. My soil is loam, but after three decades of wheat-maize double cropping, the potassium is getting low. A soil test I did through the county station in 2021 showed medium phosphorus and declining potassium, so I have been adjusting my formula since then instead of just using whatever the dealer pushes.

Right now it is early March, and my winter wheat is at the returning-green stage. Last year I got 500 kg/mu on the wheat and 600 kg/mu on the maize. The wheat was disappointing because I tried to save money by cutting the jointing-stage urea top-dressing down to only 8 kg per mu. Never again. A bad harvest costs far more than an extra bag of fertilizer. This year I will put 20 kg of urea per mu at returning green, and another 15 kg per mu at jointing in mid-April. Before sowing last October I already applied 50 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as basal. Counting that in, my wheat will get about 22 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 7 kg of potassium per mu. I know the nitrogen is on the high side, but with compound fertilizer at roughly 190 yuan per 50-kg bag and urea at 120 yuan per bag, wasting a little fertilizer is still safer than an empty grain head. For water, I will irrigate three times: returning green, jointing, and grain filling. The well pump costs me about 30 yuan per mu each time, so that is 540 yuan total for wheat water, but without it the yield collapses. I will spray a herbicide once in early spring for winter weeds, and if I see rust or aphids in May, I will add one spray of fungicide-insecticide mix. I always rotary till after maize harvest to prepare a good seedbed for wheat.

For the summer maize on the same 6 mu: after wheat harvest in early June, I will no-till plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed at about 2.5 kg per mu. There is no time to plough between wheat harvest and maize sowing, and no-tillage saves diesel anyway. I will put 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15 compound in the seed furrow at planting, then top-dress with 25 kg per mu of urea at the 12-leaf big-trumpet stage. That works out to about 17 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: right after sowing if June is dry, at big trumpet in July, and at flowering in August if the rain fails. For chemicals, I will spray a pre-emergence herbicide immediately after sowing, and I will watch the neighbors — if corn borer moths are thick and they are spraying at big trumpet, I will spray too. So two pesticide applications total. If the weather cooperates, I expect 650 kg/mu.

My total input budget for fertilizer, water, and chemicals for both crops is about 3,200 yuan. That leaves room for hiring one worker at 120 yuan per day during the harvest rush if my son is busy at the factory. I thought about trying one of the new coated urea products the dealer showed me, but at 240 yuan per bag it is not worth the risk on my whole field. Maybe next year if Old Wang across the lane gets good results.
